title: MinFlyout configuration
description: Contents of %APPDATA%\MinFlyout\config.jsonc. The file is JSONC: comments and trailing commas are allowed.

monitorSelector.description: One screen: the monitor number from the flyout caption (1, 2, ...), "primary", "secondary", a device name such as "DISPLAY2", or a resolution such as "3840x2160".

zone.description: A rectangle in percent of the reference area (see useWorkArea).

left.description: Left edge in percent of the monitor.

top.description: Top edge in percent of the monitor.

width.description: Width in percent of the monitor.

height.description: Height in percent of the monitor.

monitors.description: Screens this layout is offered on. Omit it for all of them; entries may be mixed. A screen without a single matching layout is left out of the flyout.

zones.description: The tiles of this layout. Meant to tile the screen without overlapping.

$schema.description: Path or URL of this schema; ignored by MinFlyout.

hoverDelayMs.description: How long the pointer must rest on the minimize button before the flyout opens.

closeGraceMs.description: Grace period before the flyout closes again after the pointer leaves it.

showBuiltinItems.description: Show the built-in text items (minimize, notification area, always on top, ...) below the layouts.

useWorkArea.description: true: percentages refer to the work area (without the taskbar). false: to the full monitor area.

showAllMonitors.description: true: draw one row per monitor, so a window can be moved across screens. false: only the monitor the window is on.

uiScale.description: Size factor of the flyout, on top of the scaling Windows already does for the screen resolution. 1.0 is the normal size; around 1.4 is a good starting point on a small laptop panel. Fonts, paddings and miniatures grow together, and the factor is reduced where the result would not fit on the screen.

buttonDetection.description: How the minimize button is located. auto: ask the window and compute the position when it stays silent. hittest: only ask - a window with its own title bar is then not detected. computed: never ask, always compute. Written in lower case here; MinFlyout itself ignores the case.

traceDetection.description: Log every gate of the detection, not just the successful ones - answers where a mouse movement dies. One line per change, and only in a build with the logging macros compiled in.

logToFile.description: Also write the debug log to minflyout.log next to this file. Only has an effect in builds with logging compiled in.

watchConfig.description: Watch this file and reload it as soon as it is saved. Turn it off if %APPDATA% lives on a network share that reports no changes; the tray menu command "Reload configuration" keeps working either way.

layouts.description: Layouts offered in the flyout. Each one is drawn as a miniature of the monitor. An empty array hides the miniature area; a missing property falls back to the built-in layouts.

touch.description: Dragging a window into a zone with the finger: pick the window up by its title bar, rest the finger in the trigger field, and the zones unfold across the screen.

enabled.description: Whether dragging a window into a zone by finger is offered at all.

alsoMouse.description: React to a window dragged with the mouse as well. Off by default - with a mouse the flyout is the shorter way; useful for trying the overlay out on a machine without a touchscreen.

dwellMs.description: How long the finger must rest in the trigger field before the zones unfold. Too short and merely carrying a window across the middle of the screen opens them.

trigger.description: Where the trigger field sits, in percent of the same reference area the zones use. It is only on screen while a window is actually being dragged.

layouts.description: Layouts offered while dragging. The first one matching the monitor is the one that shows - there is a single drop target, not a menu. Use "monitors" to give a tablet one arrangement upright and another on its side. A missing property falls back to the layouts of the flyout.

resize.description: Resizing a window in steps. Windows can put a window into half a screen and it can maximize one vertically; between those there is nothing that means "a bit wider". These are four ways to say it - a modifier and a click on the border, the wheel over it, a hotkey, and a row of buttons at the top of the flyout - and they all move the edges by "stepPx" pixels.

enabled.description: Whether step resizing is offered at all. false switches off all four routes at once.

stepPx.description: How far one step moves an edge, in pixels.

borderModifiers.description: Ctrl plus a click on a window border grows it, Shift plus a click shrinks it. On the left or right border that changes the width and leaves the centre alone, on the top or bottom the height. Holding Alt as well moves only the edge that was clicked.

wheel.description: Turning the wheel over a window border moves that one edge. No modifier; a corner moves both of its edges.

followEdge.description: Move the pointer along with the edge that has just moved, so the next click or notch lands on it without aiming again. It travels by however far the edge really went - shorter than a step where the screen stopped it, and not at all where the step ended in a maximize. Applies to the border and wheel gestures, not to the full-width double click.

doubleClickMaximizes.description: Double clicking the left or right border stretches the window across the full width of the screen, and back - the counterpart of the vertical maximize Windows already does on the upper and lower border.

hotkeys.description: Register Ctrl+Alt+Left / Right to narrow and widen the foreground window, Ctrl+Alt+Up / Down to shorten and lengthen it, and Ctrl+Alt+Shift+Right to toggle the full screen width. A combination somebody else already owns simply stays unavailable.

toolbar.description: Draw the row of resize buttons at the top of the flyout.
